content:
We need to return mapped_rxn and template_id for the template that when applied to the molecule reproduces the sulfonamide formation retrosynthetic step. Input from previous task: make_7_lvl2-apply_template-2 gave precursors list: [["CC(C)(C)OC(=O)Nc1ccc(N)cc1", "O=C(O)C=Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1"]]. So the target molecule is presumably the product of those two precursors reacting: amine (tert-butyl carbamate attached to aniline?) Actually first precursor: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)Nc1ccc(N)cc1 is a protected aniline (tert-butoxycarbonyl protected amine attached to aniline with an extra NH2? Wait structure: t-Boc protected aniline? It is t-Boc attached to an aniline with an extra NH? Actually N attached to carbonyl and aromatic ring with an NH substituent. Second precursor: O=C(O)C=Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1 is a sulfonyl chloride attached to aromatic ring with a cinnamic acid? Actually O=C(O)C=Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1 is a cinnamic acid with sulfonyl chloride substituent.

The retrosynthetic step: combine amine and sulfonyl chloride to form sulfonamide. So template is sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide). Need to find template ID that matches this transformation. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional groups broken/formed? The functional groups broken: sulfonyl chloride (S(=O)(=O)Cl) is a sulfonyl chloride functional group. Is that in list? Not directly; maybe "acyl chloride" but not sulfonyl chloride. Could use bonds broken: S-Cl broken, S-N formed. We attempted bonds but need correct format: bonds are specified as "atom1-atom2" using atomic numbers? The format expects something like "6-6" meaning bond between two atoms of atomic numbers? Actually example: "6-6", "6-8". So they refer to bond order? Not sure. Might be atomic numbers of atoms involved. Hard.

Alternative: maybe we can directly get template by ID from known dataset? Could guess template ID? Not.

We could try to apply template search without criteria: maybe we can search for templates that match the product? But we need template that when applied to product yields those precursors. Could use apply_template? Actually we have product SMILES? The product is the molecule from earlier task? The input to make_7_lvl2-apply_template-2 was the product? The answer gave precursors list. So product SMILES is likely the target molecule: combine them yields something. Let's reconstruct product SMILES: The amine part: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)Nc1ccc(N)cc1 (tert-butoxycarbonyl protected aniline with extra NH? Actually there is N attached to carbonyl and aromatic ring, plus an extra N on ring). The sulfonyl chloride part: O=C(O)C=Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1. When they react, the sulfonyl chloride reacts with the amine (the protected amine? The N attached to carbonyl is not nucleophilic; the free aniline NH2 is nucleophilic). So product would be sulfonamide linking the aromatic amine to sulfonyl group, plus the other groups unchanged. So product SMILES maybe: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)Nc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(C=C(C(=O)O) )cc2)cc1? Actually the sulfonyl chloride attaches to the aniline NH (the free NH). So product SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)Nc1ccc(N)cc1 with N attached to sulfonyl? Wait the aniline has two nitrogens: one is the carbamate N (attached to carbonyl) and also part of aromatic ring? Actually the SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N c1ccc(N)cc1. The N after carbonyl is attached to aromatic carbon (anilide). That N is part of the amide linking to aromatic ring; the aromatic ring also has an NH substituent (c1ccc(N)cc1). So there is a free NH on the ring. That will react with sulfonyl chloride. So product SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)Nc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(C=C(C(=O)O) )cc2)cc1. Let's generate approximate SMILES: "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)Nc1ccc(N)cc1" + sulfonyl part: "S(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=C(C(=O)O))cc2". Connect via N-S bond: replace the free N with N-S(=O)(=O)... So product SMILES: "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)Nc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=C(C(=O)O))cc2)cc1". Need proper SMILES: "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)Nc1ccc(N)cc1" becomes "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)Nc1ccc(N)cc1". To attach sulfonyl: "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)Nc1ccc(N)cc1" -> replace N with N(S(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=C(C(=O)O))cc2). So final: "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)Nc1ccc(N(S(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=C(C(=O)O))cc2))cc1". Let's use that as product SMILES.

Now we need to find template that when applied to product yields the two precursors. Could search templates that match product and produce those precursors. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional groups broken: maybe "sulfonamide" broken? Actually forward reaction: sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So reverse (retrosynthesis) breaks S-N bond and forms S-Cl? Actually the template for retrosynthesis would break S-N bond and form S-Cl (i.e., generate sulfonyl chloride). So functional groups broken: sulfonamide (product) broken to sulfonyl chloride (precursor). So functional_groups_broken: "sulfonamide". functional_groups_formed: maybe "sulfonyl_chloride"? Not in list. But we can break sulfonamide and form sulfonyl chloride? Not available.

Maybe we can just retrieve template by ID from known dataset? Could guess template ID like 12345? Not reliable.

Alternative: Use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching to test candidate templates? But we need template ID first.

Maybe the template catalog includes a template for sulfonamide formation with ID we can guess by searching with bonds broken/formed using atomic numbers. The bond broken is S-N (bond between S (atomic number 16) and N (7)). So bond broken "16-7". Bond formed is S-Cl (16-17). So we can search with bonds_broken ["16-7"], bonds_formed ["16-17"]. Let's try.
